analysis.title: Asia Open - Circle the winners
key_insights: Markets repriced aggressively after the US midterm result. Equities split, with Mag7 rallying on a presumed slowdown in AI capex while semiconductors fell on the same presumption.
SPX rose 1.58%, its best single day since August, led by Mag7 constituents. SOX fell 3.13% on the day and is down 23% over the past 30 days.
Equity vol dropped as peak event risk passed. NFP implied moves compressed to SPX 0.71%, QQQ 1.3% and IWM 0.98%.
ESZ6 closed above the CTA trigger of $7,670 that flips systematic positioning long, which points to likely systematic buying on Thursday.

Global fixed income rallied with the drop in oil, and UST yields fell 8bps, led by the belly of the curve. The market is described as structurally short and tactically long, driven largely by systematic funds.
Citi's US Rates Strategy desk initiated a tactical long in 30y breakevens because valuation looks disconnected from solid risk asset performance, relatively dovish policy and above-average growth.
The Treasury quarterly refunding matched expectations and kept nominal coupon sizes unchanged. The coupon guidance opened the door to auction size adjustments in 2027.

Crude fell about 8% on the day, with WTI at $89 and Brent at $95. Brent is nearly 20% lower since Friday. Citi's commodities strategist sees choppy conditions until 2027 and a bearish broader outlook for oil.
US diesel stockpiles fell below 100 million barrels for the first time since 2003. Gold rose 3.4% back above $4,000, its largest gain since mid-August.
The dollar sold off initially on the Dem sweep, on lighter AI-driven inflows and safe-haven qualities. The move was mostly short-lived as attention returned to sticky inflation and NFP on Friday.

EUR strengthened after Eurozone CPI came in line at +0.4% MoM. About 20bps of a December ECB hike is priced. LatAm currencies rallied after a Tuesday sell-off in which BRL, COP and MXN each fell more than 1%.
The Polish MPC held at 3.75% as expected. PLN rose nearly 1% after staff inflation forecasts were raised to 3.2% for 2026 and 4.2% for 2027.

Asia calendar: Citi keeps its call for a 25bp BoJ hike in December. It expects BNM to hold in November and hike 25bps in January. It sees higher October CPI in the Philippines and Thailand and lower CPI in Taiwan.

Market pricing is partial, so a hawkish surprise could lift EUR further.

macro_indicators.interpretation: There is some risk of a hike in November. The January hike may be flagged with stronger language at the November meeting.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Citi economists expect both headline and core inflation to moderate.

trade_ideas.rationale: Valuation seems to be diverging from solid risk asset performance, relatively dovish monetary policy and above-average growth.

risk_factors: Sticky inflation and the implications of upcoming US data for the Fed path, with NFP due Friday.
A more rigid regulatory backdrop and AI capex slowdown, which is pressuring semis.
Choppy oil outlook until 2027 with a bearish broader view.
Macro framework stuck between reflationary and goldilocks, which leaves systematic positioning exposed to a turn.
Treasury opened the door to auction size adjustments in 2027, a potential supply risk for the long end.
vol_and_positioning: Equity vol capitulated as peak event risk passed. NFP implied moves compressed to SPX 0.71%, QQQ 1.3% and IWM 0.98%.
SPX (ESZ6) closed above the CTA trigger at $7,670, which flips systematic positioning long and points to buying flows on Thursday.
Rates market is structurally short and tactically long, driven largely by systematic funds.
On the NY eFX desk, activity was heavy in EUR pairs. Net flows favored CZK, EUR and JPY, and outflows were tilted toward CNH, USD and DKK.
geopolitical: US midterm elections produced a Democratic sweep, which drove the cross-asset repricing. The dollar's safe-haven qualities were cited in its initial move.
Citi hosts a client call on the post-results assessment and implications for Asia.
